audit_status.source_base: Greek 1 Corinthians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for collection, travel plans, Timothy/Apollos, watchfulness, love, Stephanas household, final greetings and grace.

verses.restored: Now concerning the collection for the holy ones: just as I directed the assemblies of Galatia, so also you do.

familiar.text: Now concerning the collection for the saints, as I have given order to the churches of Galatia, even so do ye.

modern.text: Now about the collection for the saints, you are to do as I directed the churches of Galatia:

original.text: Περὶ δὲ τῆς λογείας τῆς εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους, ὥσπερ διέταξα ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῆς Γαλατίας, οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ποιήσατε.

verses.restored: On the first day of every week, let each of you set aside by oneself, storing up whatever one may prosper, so that collections may not happen when I come.

familiar.text: Upon the first day of the week let every one of you lay by him in store, as God hath prospered him, that there be no gatherings when I come.

modern.text: On the first day of every week, each of you should set aside a portion of his income, saving it up, so that when I come no collections will be needed.

original.text: κατὰ μίαν ⸀σαββάτου ἕκαστος ὑμῶν παρʼ ἑαυτῷ τιθέτω θησαυρίζων ὅ τι ⸀ἐὰν εὐοδῶται, ἵνα μὴ ὅταν ἔλθω τότε λογεῖαι γίνωνται.

verses.restored: When I arrive, whomever you approve through letters, I will send these to carry your grace-gift to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And when I come, whomsoever ye shall approve by your letters, them will I send to bring your liberality unto Jerusalem.

modern.text: Then, on my arrival, I will send letters with those you recommend to carry your gift to Jerusalem.

original.text: ὅταν δὲ παραγένωμαι, οὓς ⸀ἐὰν δοκιμάσητε διʼ ἐπιστολῶν, τούτους πέμψω ἀπενεγκεῖν τὴν χάριν ὑμῶν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ·

verses.restored: And if it is suitable for me also to go, they will go with me.

familiar.text: And if it be meet that I go also, they shall go with me.

modern.text: And if it is advisable for me to go also, they can travel with me. Paul’s Travel Plans (Romans 15:23–33)

original.text: ἐὰν δὲ ⸂ἄξιον ᾖ⸃ τοῦ κἀμὲ πορεύεσθαι, σὺν ἐμοὶ πορεύσονται.

verses.restored: I will come to you when I pass through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia,

familiar.text: Now I will come unto you, when I shall pass through Macedonia: for I do pass through Macedonia.

modern.text: After I go through Macedonia, however, I will come to you; for I will be going through Macedonia.

original.text: Ἐλεύσομαι δὲ πρὸς ὑμᾶς ὅταν Μακεδονίαν διέλθω, Μακεδονίαν γὰρ διέρχομαι,

verses.restored: and perhaps I will remain with you, or even winter, so that you may send me forward wherever I may go.

familiar.text: And it may be that I will abide, yea, and winter with you, that ye may bring me on my journey whithersoever I go.

modern.text: Perhaps I will stay with you awhile, or even spend the winter, so that you can help me on my journey, wherever I go.

original.text: πρὸς ὑμᾶς δὲ τυχὸν ⸀παραμενῶ ἢ ⸀καὶ παραχειμάσω, ἵνα ὑμεῖς με προπέμψητε οὗ ἐὰν πορεύωμαι.

verses.restored: For I do not want to see you now in passing, for I hope to remain some time with you, if the Lord permits.

familiar.text: For I will not see you now by the way; but I trust to tarry a while with you, if the Lord permit.

modern.text: For I do not want to see you now only in passing; I hope to spend some time with you, if the Lord permits.

original.text: οὐ θέλω γὰρ ὑμᾶς ἄρτι ἐν παρόδῳ ἰδεῖν, ἐλπίζω ⸀γὰρ χρόνον τινὰ ἐπιμεῖναι πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἐὰν ὁ κύριος ⸀ἐπιτρέψῃ.

verses.restored: But I will remain in Ephesus until Pentecost,

familiar.text: But I will tarry at Ephesus until Pentecost.

modern.text: But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost,

original.text: ⸀ἐπιμενῶ δὲ ἐν Ἐφέσῳ ἕως τῆς πεντηκοστῆς·

verses.restored: for a great and effective door has opened to me, and there are many opposing.

familiar.text: For a great door and effectual is opened unto me, and there are many adversaries.

modern.text: because a great door for effective work has opened to me, even though many oppose me. Timothy and Apollos (Philippians 2:19–30)

original.text: θύρα γάρ μοι ἀνέῳγεν μεγάλη καὶ ἐνεργής, καὶ ἀντικείμενοι πολλοί.

verses.restored: If Timothy comes, see that he may be with you without fear, for he works the work of the Lord as I also do.

familiar.text: Now if Timotheus come, see that he may be with you without fear: for he worketh the work of the Lord, as I also do.

modern.text: If Timothy comes, see to it that he has nothing to fear while he is with you, for he is doing the work of the Lord, just as I am.

original.text: Ἐὰν δὲ ἔλθῃ Τιμόθεος, βλέπετε ἵνα ἀφόβως γένηται πρὸς ὑμᾶς, τὸ γὰρ ἔργον κυρίου ἐργάζεται ὡς ⸀κἀγώ·

verses.restored: Therefore let no one despise him, but send him forward in peace, so that he may come to me; for I await him with the siblings.

familiar.text: Let no man therefore despise him: but conduct him forth in peace, that he may come unto me: for I look for him with the brethren.

modern.text: No one, then, should treat him with contempt. Send him on his way in peace so that he can return to me, for I am expecting him along with the brothers.

original.text: μή τις οὖν αὐτὸν ἐξουθενήσῃ. προπέμψατε δὲ αὐτὸν ἐν εἰρήνῃ, ἵνα ἔλθῃ πρός ⸀με, ἐκδέχομαι γὰρ αὐτὸν μετὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν.

verses.restored: Now concerning Apollos the sibling, I urged him much to come to you with the siblings, and it was not at all his will to come now; but he will come when he has opportunity.

familiar.text: As touching our brother Apollos, I greatly desired him to come unto you with the brethren: but his will was not at all to come at this time; but he will come when he shall have convenient time.

modern.text: Now about our brother Apollos: I strongly urged him to go to you with the brothers. He was not at all inclined to go now, but he will go when he has the opportunity. Concluding Exhortations

original.text: Περὶ δὲ Ἀπολλῶ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ, πολλὰ παρεκάλεσα αὐτὸν ἵνα ἔλθῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς μετὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν· καὶ πάντως οὐκ ἦν θέλημα ἵνα νῦν ἔλθῃ, ἐλεύσεται δὲ ὅταν εὐκαιρήσῃ.

verses.restored: Stay awake; stand firm in the trust; be courageous; be strong.

familiar.text: Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong.

modern.text: Be on the alert. Stand firm in the faith. Be men of courage. Be strong.

original.text: Γρηγορεῖτε, στήκετε ἐν τῇ πίστει, ἀνδρίζεσθε, κραταιοῦσθε.

verses.restored: Let all your things happen in love.

familiar.text: Let all your things be done with charity.

modern.text: Do everything in love.

original.text: πάντα ὑμῶν ἐν ἀγάπῃ γινέσθω.

verses.restored: I urge you, siblings: you know the household of Stephanas, that it is firstfruit of Achaia, and that they appointed themselves into service for the holy ones.

familiar.text: I beseech you, brethren, (ye know the house of Stephanas, that it is the firstfruits of Achaia, and that they have addicted themselves to the ministry of the saints,)

modern.text: You know that Stephanas and his household were the first converts in Achaia, and they have devoted themselves to the service of the saints. Now I urge you, brothers,

original.text: Παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί· οἴδατε τὴν οἰκίαν Στεφανᾶ, ὅτι ἐστὶν ἀπαρχὴ τῆς Ἀχαΐας καὶ εἰς διακονίαν τοῖς ἁγίοις ἔταξαν ἑαυτούς·

verses.restored: That you also be subject to such ones and to everyone working together and laboring.

familiar.text: That ye submit yourselves unto such, and to every one that helpeth with us, and laboureth.

modern.text: to submit to such as these, and to every fellow worker and laborer.

original.text: ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς ὑποτάσσησθε τοῖς τοιούτοις καὶ παντὶ τῷ συνεργοῦντι καὶ κοπιῶντι.

verses.restored: I rejoice over the arrival of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus, because these filled up what was lacking from you,

familiar.text: I am glad of the coming of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus: for that which was lacking on your part they have supplied.

modern.text: I am glad that Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus have arrived, because they have supplied what was lacking from you.

original.text: χαίρω δὲ ἐπὶ τῇ παρουσίᾳ Στεφανᾶ καὶ Φορτουνάτου καὶ Ἀχαϊκοῦ, ὅτι τὸ ⸀ὑμέτερον ὑστέρημα οὗτοι ἀνεπλήρωσαν,

verses.restored: for they refreshed my spirit and yours. Therefore recognize such ones.

familiar.text: For they have refreshed my spirit and yours: therefore acknowledge ye them that are such.

modern.text: For they refreshed my spirit and yours as well. Show your appreciation, therefore, to such men. Signature and Final Greetings (Colossians 4:15–18; 2 Thessalonians 3:16–18)

original.text: ἀνέπαυσαν γὰρ τὸ ἐμὸν πνεῦμα καὶ τὸ ὑμῶν. ἐπιγινώσκετε οὖν τοὺς τοιούτους.

verses.restored: The assemblies of Asia greet you. Aquila and Prisca greet you much in the Lord, with the assembly in their house.

familiar.text: The churches of Asia salute you. Aquila and Priscilla salute you much in the Lord, with the church that is in their house.

modern.text: The churches in the province of Asia send you greetings. Aquila and Prisca greet you warmly in the Lord, and so does the church that meets at their house.

original.text: Ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς αἱ ἐκκλησίαι τῆς Ἀσίας. ⸀ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς ἐν κυρίῳ πολλὰ Ἀκύλας καὶ ⸀Πρίσκα σὺν τῇ κατʼ οἶκον αὐτῶν ἐκκλησίᾳ.

verses.restored: All the siblings greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.

familiar.text: All the brethren greet you. Greet ye one another with an holy kiss.

modern.text: All the brothers here send you greetings. Greet one another with a holy kiss.

original.text: ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς οἱ ἀδελφοὶ πάντες. ἀσπάσασθε ἀλλήλους ἐν φιλήματι ἁγίῳ.

verses.restored: The greeting is by my hand, Paul's.

familiar.text: The salutation of me Paul with mine own hand.

modern.text: This greeting is in my own hand—Paul.

original.text: Ὁ ἀσπασμὸς τῇ ἐμῇ χειρὶ Παύλου.

verses.restored: If anyone does not love the Lord, let that one be devoted to judgment. Marana tha.

familiar.text: If any man love not the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be Anathema Maranatha.

modern.text: If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be under a curse. Come, O Lord!

original.text: εἴ τις οὐ φιλεῖ τὸν ⸀κύριον, ἤτω ἀνάθεμα. ⸂Μαράνα θά⸃.

verses.restored: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.

familiar.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

modern.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.

original.text: ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου ⸀Ἰησοῦ μεθʼ ὑμῶν.

verses.restored: My love is with all of you in Messiah Jesus. Amen.

familiar.text: My love be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.

modern.text: My love be with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.

original.text: ἡ ἀγάπη μου μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν ἐν Χριστῷ ⸀Ἰησοῦ.

translation_notes: Chapter 16 grounds the letter's spiritual teaching in practical solidarity: collection for Jerusalem, travel, recognition of servants, and love governing all.
Marana tha is preserved as Aramaic liturgical cry, often understood as Our Lord, come / Our Lord has come.
